text: Jaffle Shop's marketing team now runs email campaigns through a third-party platform that exports a CSV, with no native Snowflake connector and no API this platform has already built against.

This is a genuinely common real scenario, not a contrived one — a vendor export, a partner's manual file drop, a legacy system with no modern API. A production-grade platform needs a real answer for exactly this case.

Two Python tools handle this job: pandas, already familiar from this path's data work, reads and cleans the CSV. snowflake-connector-python, a genuinely new library introduced honestly here, connects to Snowflake and loads it.

dbt can't do this part itself — every dbt model starts from data already inside Snowflake, reading through source or ref, never from a file sitting on a laptop. Getting the file in, in the first place, is a separate, upstream job.

This is Layer 3 of the five-layer architecture from Lesson 2, sitting between Snowflake's RAW schema and the dbt models that will eventually build on top of whatever this script lands. Next: writing the real script.
